div.head: Ordal Inscr.
div.ab: Dom be haten ísene an[d] wætre.
DOM BE HATEN ÍSENE AND WÆTRE
Gesetz (Gottesgericht?) vom heissen Eisen und [siedenden] Wasser.
Law (judgment of God?) concerning hot iron and [boiling] water.

div.note: Liebermann's text is from H (Textus Roffensis f. 32, after Forfang 1, in the same hand, c. 1120), the same manuscript as the modern edition. The heading is in red. Since clause 1 begins with ‘And’, the beginning is lacking, and the heading, which presents this fragment of a royal law as an independent work, is therefore not original. Liebermann dates it c. 936–58 or up to c. 1000. In the Quadripartitus it follows VI As. Clause number standardised from ‘Ord. Inscr.’.; F: corrected against Liebermann, Gesetze I (date in the running heads), October 2026 (was “c.936–58, or c.1000; ?c. 930 (Wormald)”, now “c.936–58 or –c.1000 (Liebermann); ?c.930 (Wormald)”); BQ: page of each of Liebermann’s texts and of his German, checked against Liebermann, Gesetze I (column heads, read twice), October 2026 (e.g. was “(empty)”, now “H 386; Q 386; German 386”; 13 rows of Ordal)
